name: Manage API
description:
This is the REST Manage API that can be used by Ensighten Manage customers.

There are currently two ways to authenticate through the Manage API: API Key and Username / Password.

All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Calls made over plain HTTP will fail. You must authenticate for all requests.

Supported Entities

  • Spaces

  • Publish Paths

  • Deployments

  • Conditions

  • Data Definitions

  • Event Definitions

  • Users

  • Roles

  • SCIM 2.0

  • Git

  • TDN

resourceGroups.name: API Key
resourceGroups.description:
To create a new API Key, navigate to the "API Keys" page in the Admin section of your Manage account. When creating an API Key, you will need to provide a Name and assign relevant Roles to the API Key.

After saving, you will receive your API Key. This will be the only time the API key is visible, so ensure you record it securely. If lost, you can reset your API key at any time.

API Request

API Key authentication requires passing the API Key in every request using the X-API-Key header.

Example
X-API-Key: ens_01hL1o3iAHKHObEfLM0JKk9hfUYp6KOvsAbY

Note: The authentication endpoints (/auth/token) do not support API Key authentication. If you are using an API Key, you can directly authenticate your requests without needing a token.

resourceGroups.name: Authentication
resourceGroups.description:
Requests using a username and password for authentication follow the Resource Owner Password Flow of the OAuth 2.0 specification.

API Request

Once a token has been retrieved using the /auth/token process below, include it in all API calls using the Authorization header.

Example
Authorization: Bearer 2YotnFZFEjr1zCsicMWpAA

actions.name: Username/Password/MultiFactor Authentication
actions.description:
In order to gain an access token for use with the API a call must be made using a valid account name, user name, and password. If the account is MFA configured, MFA verification code is also needed.

The Authorization header contains the Base64 encoded concatenation of the account name, user name, and password. For example, the value mycompany:joe:mypassword would be encoded and used in the header value.

The MultiFactorAuthentication header is needed if the account is MFA configured which is a 6 digits number that is created from Google Authentication App on the phone.

The grant_type of password must be included in the body.

actions.name: Refreshing Access Tokens
actions.description:
All access tokens granted will automatically expire after the timeframe specified when retrieving the token, so all developer code must cater for refreshing tokens.

To request a new token, provide the Authorization header (see Username/Password Authentication) along with the parameter of grant_type=refresh_token as well as refresh_token with the token supplied in the previous token grant must be included in the body.

resourceGroups.name: Publish Paths
resourceGroups.description:
CRUD operations with Publish Paths.

For further details or guidance on configuring Publish Path settings, please consult our Help Center article available here.

Publish Path specific fields

Field Required Description Valid Values
name Y The name of the publish path A name up to 30 characters
codeGen N Code generation settings for the publish path An object containing codegen configuration (see below)

Codegen specific fields

These fields are nested within the codeGen object. If the codeGen object is omitted on create, the defaults indicated below will be applied. On update, only the fields provided will be modified.

Field Required Description Valid Values
namespace N Parent object reference for the publish path A name up to 30 characters

Defaults to "Bootstrapper" if none provided
versionId N The id of the Bootstrap version name. Versions V1 through V8 are deprecated (see the Bootstrap Version Support Policy for details). 1 - v1_20190727
2 - v2_20191031
3 - v3_20200123
5 - v4_20200406
6 - v5_20200514
7 - v6_20201029
8 - v7_20220512
9 - v8_20220915
10 - v9_20230706
11 - v10
12 - v11
13 - v12
14 - v13 (default)
minificationLevelId N Affects how the Manage deployed code is compiled 1 - Whitespace (default)
2 - Simple
languageId N ECMAScript language version 1 - ECMASCRIPT_2018
2 - ECMASCRIPT_2019
3 - ECMASCRIPT_2020 (default)
sriHashAlgorithmId N Subresource Integrity (SRI) 1 - Disabled (default)
2 - Enabled [SHA-256]
nexusContextId N Nexus Context 1 - Disabled (default)

parameters.description: Get the requested fields for the resulting deployments.
parameters.example: id, name, spaceId, spaceName, appName, isCustomApp, status, executionTime, lastAction, labels, ruleId, comments, dependentDeployments, conditionIds, code, creationDate, modifyDate

parameters.description: Sort the resulting deployments by the given field name. Acceptable field names are 'name', 'appName', 'spaceName' and 'lastActionDate'. A '-' prefix indicates sort in descending order.

Filters deployments based on the given parameters. Acceptable parameters in this object are

  • "id" (number) ... A single deployment Id.

  • "name" (string) ... A single deployment name.

  • "spaceId" (string) ... Comma-separated list of space Ids.

  • "publishPathId" (string) ... Comma-separated list of publish path Ids.

  • "eventId" (string) ... Comma-separated list of event Ids.

  • "labels" (object) ... List of label object keys and allowed values. Passing no values or null will filter on just the label key.

  • "appId" (string) ... Comma-separated list of app Ids.

  • "conditionId" (string) ... Comma-separated list of condition Ids. A deployment matches a condition if it
    1. Directly uses the condition
    2. Uses an event that requires the condition, or
    3. Is in a Space that mandates the condition

  • "code" (string) ... A single string to search for in the deployment's code.

  • "enableDisableStatus" (string) ... Array of strings that filters deployments by status using pattern matching. Can use category values like 'enabled', 'disabled', 'deleted', 'archived' to match all states in that category, or specific values like 'disabled_published', 'archived_uncommitted' to match exact states.

  • "live" (boolean) ... 'true' to filter for deployments enabled and published.

  • "includeGlobalSynchronous" (boolean) ... When true, deployments using the All Pages - Blocking (Synchronous) condition are included in the results. This combines with conditionId to produce four outcomes:
    1. true and conditionId provided - returns deployments matching any of the given conditions or the All Pages - Blocking (Synchronous) condition.
    2. true and conditionId omitted - returns only deployments with the All Pages - Blocking (Synchronous) condition.
    3. false/omitted and conditionId provided - returns only deployments matching the given conditions, excluding the All Pages - Blocking (Synchronous) condition.
    4. false/omitted and conditionId omitted - applies no condition-based filtering.

  • "sinceCreated" (date string) ... To get deployments that were created on or after a date in GMT, e.g. 2014-08-07.

  • "untilCreated" (date string) ... To get deployments that were created before or on a date in GMT.

  • "sinceUpdated" (date string) ... To get deployments that were updated on or after a date in GMT.

  • "untilUpdated" (date string) ... To get deployments that were updated before or on a date in GMT.

CRUD operations with Conditions.

Important Condition specific fields

Field Description Valid Values

Condition-value specific fields

A condition can have one or more condition-values, each of which is defined as an object with the following (required) properties

Field Description Valid Values
typeId Indicates the type of the condition parameter 2 (Host)
4 (Path)
7 (Protocol)
10 (Query Pair)
11 (Hash Fragment)
16 (Platform)
18 (DateTime)
19 (Geocode)
20 (IP Address)
26 (Browser)
27 (Do Not Track)
28 (Date Recurrence)
30 (Data Definition)
31 (Query Param)
32 (Query Value)
33 (Test URLs)
35 (Threat Type)
value Indicates the value for the condition (as a string) see examples below
comparatorId Indicates the comparator to use for mapping the type to value For Threat Type (typeId: 35)
  • 34 (include) - Matches any selected Threat Type(s)
  • 35 (exclude) - Does not match any selected Threat Type(s)
  • 36 (include all) - Matches all selected Threat Type(s)
  • 37 (exclude all) - Does not match all selected Threat Type(s)
  • 38 (include exact) - Matches exactly the selected Threat Type(s)
  • 39 (exclude exact) - Does not match exactly the selected Threat Type(s)

For Date Recurrence (typeId: 28)
  • 28 (is in list)
  • With the list as numbers with the mapping 0=Sunday, 1=Monday and so on

For Browser (typeId: 26)
  • 26 (is in list)

For Do Not Track (typeId: 27)
  • 27 (is)
  • With the value being 'T' or 'F' to indicate True or False

For IP Address (typeId: 20)
  • 16 (equals)
  • 17 (is greater than)
  • 18 (is less than)

For Geocode (typeId: 19)
  • 15 (is in list)

For DateTime (typeId: 18)
  • 12 (is before)
  • 13 (is after)

For Platform (typeId: 16)
  • 14 (is in list)

For All Other Types
  • 0 (No-op)
  • 1 (Equals)
  • 2 (Contains)
  • 3 (Matches RegEx)
  • 4 (Begins with)
  • 5 (Ends with)
modifierIds Indicates the modifiers to use on the values There are only two acceptable values:
1 (negation/not), 2 (ignore case)

For example, for condition value which host contains test.com or TEST.COM or Test.com would be:

    {
        "typeId": 2,
        "value": "test.com",
        "comparatorId": 2,
        "modifierIds": [2]
    }

And for condition value which host does not contain test.com would be:

    {
        "typeId": 2,
        "value": "test.com",
        "comparatorId": 2,
        "modifierIds": [1]
    }

Label specific fields

resources An array of unique identifiers for the resources. Each resource is referenced by an Ensighten Resource Name (ERN in the format: ern:ens:manage::{resource-type}:{resource-id}

Ensighten Resource Names (ERNs)

Ensighten Resource Names (ERNs) provide a standardized way to uniquely identify resources across the Ensighten platform. Every ERN follows a consistent structure that encodes the namespace, service, resource type, and unique identifier.

Format

ern:ens:manage::{resource-type}:{resource-id}

  • {resource-type} - type of resource (e.g., deployment, condition, space)

  • {resource-id} - unique ID for the resource

Examples

  • Condition:

    ern:ens:manage::condition:{condition-id}

  • Data Definition:

    ern:ens:manage::datadefinition:{datadefinition-id}

  • Deployment:

    ern:ens:manage::deployment:space/{space-id}/deployment/{deployment-id}

  • Event:

    ern:ens:manage::event:{event-id}

resourceGroups.name: SCIM 2.0
resourceGroups.description:
SCIM2 (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) is a specification that automates user and group identity provisioning across cloud-based applications and services using SSO and Identity Providers. These SCIM2 API's enable user and group management through dedicated resources. SCIM follows RESTful principles, using HTTP methods with schema-defined payloads that include attributes and values.

While using the SCIM APIs, set the value of the Accept header as application/scim+json.

It is suggested to authenticate with the APIs using Authorization: Bearer ens_01.... However, the use of X-API-KEY: ens_01... is also supported.

SCIM 2.0 User specific fields

Field Description Valid Values
userName Unique identifier for the user Up to 255 characters; cannot include <, >, :, ~, +, or spaces
name User's name object containing givenName and familyName Object with givenName and familyName fields
emails User's email addresses Array of email objects with value and type fields, only a single work or primary work email is supported
active Whether the user is active Boolean value (true or false)
groups Groups the user belongs to Array of group objects with value fields, value must be the group id (the same id used by /scim2/Groups/{id}); group names are not accepted and result in a 400 error. Responses also include a display sub-attribute containing the group name

SCIM 2.0 Group specific fields

Note: The Group resource is a SCIM 2.0 object that maps to the values from underlying Manage Role resources.

Field Description Valid Values
displayName The display name of the group Up to 255 characters; displayName should only contain alphanumerics (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), periods, commas, +, =, @, _, or -
members The users who belong to this group Array of user objects with value fields, value should be the users ID

SCIM 2.0 Field Restrictions

Fields that are not mentioned in the tables above are not supported. Some fields may contain placeholder values. For example, "displayName" will always return the users givenName + familyName instead of a dedicated displayName value. This is because this field is part of a standard SCIM response that may be expected. Additionally, updates on the following fields are not supported:

  • Users userName

  • Groups displayName

resourceGroups.name: Additional documentation
resourceGroups.description:
This section contains additional documentation on request and response values.

Http Response Codes

Code Text Description
200 OK Success!
201 Created Successful creation of a resource.
204 No Content The request was processed successfully, but no response body is needed.
400 Bad Request The request was invalid or cannot be otherwise served. This usually means malformed syntax or a bad query.
401 Unauthorized Authentication credentials were missing or incorrect.
403 Forbidden The request is understood, but it has been refused or access is not allowed.
404 Not Found The URI requested is invalid or the resource requested, such as a deployment, does not exists. Search endpoints also return this code when no records match the given search criteria (including when no records of that type exist in the account yet); in that case treat the 404 as an empty result set.
406 Not Acceptable Requested representation not available for the resource, such as the Accept header is not valid.
412 Precondition Failed The request assumes that a pre-condition is met, but is not in this case.
415 Unsupported Media Type The request includes data that is not support, such as the Content-Type header is invalid.
422 Unprocessable Entity The data included with the request could not be processed. This usually would mean that invalid JSON was included.
429 Too Many Requests Returned when a request cannot be served due to rate limit having been exhausted for the resource.
500 Internal Server Error Something is broken on our end.
502 Bad Gateway The service is down or being upgraded.
503 Service Unavailable The service is up, but overloaded with requests. Try again later.

General Error Response

When an error occurs, the API returns a JSON response body with the following structure:

{
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Bad Request",
    "description": "A human-readable description of what went wrong."
}

The code field mirrors the HTTP status code. The message field is a standard HTTP status text. The description field provides specific detail about the error to help identify the cause.

Rate Limiting

To prevent abuse, it is standard practice to add some sort of rate limiting to an API. RFC 6585 introduced a HTTP status code 429 Too Many Requests to accommodate this.

  • HTTP Headers and Response Codes

    New Http headers will be returned with calls that are utilizing rate limiting. Make sure you inspect these headers, as they provide important information regarding limiting.

    For endpoints that are utilizing limiting the following headers will be returned with requests. In the event that the limit has been exceeded, the returned Http status code will be 429 - Too many requests.

    • X-Rate-Limit-Limit: the rate limit ceiling for that given request
    • X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: the number of requests left for the defined window
    • X-Rate-Limit-Reset: the remaining window, in seconds, before the rate limit resets

    The response will look something like this:

        {
        "code": 429,
        "message": "Rate limit ceiling reached",
        "description": "The maximum number of requests (50) for this resource has been reached. It will be reset in 350 seconds."
    }

  • Endpoints

    The Manage API has applied rate limiting to certain actions. The following table outlines which calls are limited:

    Endpoint Method Scope Limit
    /manage/spaces/{id}/publish PUT Account 5/hour

Fields Parameter

The fields request parameter defines what data is returned in the response. This allows caller to pair down the data to only which is needed and thus saves vital resources as the data is transferred over the wire. The fields parameter is a comma delimited list of fields to include in the response and allows for hierarchical reference to objects. Each resource that allows field selection will define and document how to use it. For instance, take the following JSON for a fictitious object.

{
    "id": 100,
    "name": "Bob Smith",
    "address": {
        "street": "112  Main Street",
        "city": "Anytown",
        "state": "California",
        "postal": "91741"
    }
}

Examples:

  • If the user wants just the id and name they would use "id, name)" for the definition which would result in the following json:

    {
    "id": 100,
    "name": "Bob Smith",
}

  • If the user wants just the id, name, and post code they would use "id, name, address(postal)" for the definition which would result in the following json:

    {
    "id": 100,
    "name": "Bob Smith",
    "address": {
        "postal": "91741"
    }
}

Sorting

The sort request parameter defines how the data is sorted before being returned. Each resource that allows sorting will define and document which fields are supported. The sort parameter is a comma delimited list of fields to sort on. If the field is preceded by a "-" character then it is assumed to be a descending sort. If the field is preceded by a "+" character or no sort character then it is presumed to be an ascending sort.

Examples:

  • If the user wants to have an ascending sort on the field "name", then could could define the sort option as "sort": "+name" or "sort": "name"

  • If the user wants to have an descending sort on the field "name" and an ascending sort on "address", then could could define the sort option as "sort": "-name, +address" or "sort": "-name, address"
